title: Add ref.mounted guards after awaits in PinFlowController before touching state

evidence.quote:
try {
          final ok = await pinService.verifyProfilePin(profileId, pin);

state = state.copyWith(busy: true, errorMessage: null);
        await pinService.setProfilePin(profileId, pin);

try {
      final ok = await pinService.verifyProfilePin(profileId, pin);

why: Per SM-4 (and the digest's own note that Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException), every `await` in a Notifier method must be followed by a `ref.mounted` check before touching `state`. None of the four PIN-transition handlers in this @Riverpod(keepAlive:true) notifier do this — `_handleSetup`, `_handleChange` (twice), and `_handleVerify` all assign `state = state.copyWith(...)` immediately after an `await pinService.*Pin(...)` with no guard. The confirm-step of `_handleChange` (line 350-351) is worse: it has no try/catch at all around `setProfilePin`, unlike its own sibling handlers. If the provider is invalidated/torn down while a bcrypt hash/secure-storage write is in flight (e.g. rapid navigation away, container disposal), the resulting exception is unguarded and, for the confirm-step case, has no catch clause to even convert it to a value.
recommendation: After each await in _handleSetup/_handleChange/_handleVerify, add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` before assigning state; wrap the confirm-step setProfilePin call in the same try/catch pattern used by _handleSetup.
acceptance_criteria: Every await in pin_flow_controller.dart's four handlers is followed by a ref.mounted check before state is touched
A regression test disposes the ProviderContainer mid-await and asserts no UnmountedRefException escapes
_handleChange's confirm step catches the same exception types as _handleSetup

corrections: keepAlive:true (per the file's own doc comment) defeats the 'rapid navigation away' trigger cited in the why-text; only container disposal (app teardown/tests) remains a realistic trigger. Doesn't kill the finding — rule is violated regardless of trigger frequency.
